steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You go with Manphist and the others. I'll find Hilda.
You wrench your hand from Helene's grasp without a second thought, racing up the stairs until you skid to a halt outside Hilda's door.
The corridor is a tunnel of fire, deserted and choked with swirling smoke.
You pound on the door, only to hear no answer. Instead, from within, you hear the unmistakable, metallic click of a gun being cocked.
Instinct screams that something is terribly wrong. You retreat, slipping cautiously into your own room next door.
[Study]
You make straight for the study, your fingers finding the hidden switch with practiced ease. The wall opens, revealing the secret passage.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...!! What in the—
The narrow passage is illuminated by ghostly fluorescent arrows. In their eerie glow, you see a chaos of footprints scuffing the dust, and the air hangs thick with the acrid sting of gunsmoke.
A cold dread grips you. You plunge forward, racing toward Hilda's room.
[Slow Scene Change: Hilda's Room]

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...Who's... there...
The room is a charnel house, choked with thick smoke and dancing flames.
Several guards litter the floor, their blood mingling in dark, spreading pools. A brutal gunfight has painted the scene with violence.

And there is Hilda. She lies on the cold floor, most of her clothing saturated with blood. Below her throat, a ghastly wound leaks crimson, viscous fluid. Every shallow, wet breath she takes bubbles horrifically.
Yet, her gun is still clenched in her fist, aimed shakily at the door.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Hilda!

You crash to your knees beside her, pressing torn cloth hard against the wound. Blood instantly soaks through, hot and relentless against your fingers. You can feel her life slipping away, like an unstoppable tide receding.
(CG: Death)

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I hear... ${PlayerName}...? Is that you? The lights... have all gone out...

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Listen... they found the secret passage... behind the wardrobe... in the manor...

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: That gun from before... keep it close... when the time comes... don't hesitate...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Stop talking! I'll find something to stop the bleeding!
She tries to lift a hand to stop you, but the gesture dies as a feeble twitch.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Don't... It's already too late...

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Heh... Never thought... you'd be the one with me... Not bad... Could've been much worse...
With a final, monumental effort, the one hand she can still move finds your collar and clutches it.
What are you trying to tell me?
(White Interaction Point)
A small key rests in her palm, radiating a stark, silver light. Without ceremony, she presses it firmly into your hand and gestures toward the Monolith.
Your gaze finds the device behind her. Its dark surface is broken only by a single, prominent lock. Even now, the machine stands like Death itself, cold and ruthless in the room's center.

You fit the key into the lock. The casing clicks open, revealing a breathtakingly complex web of multifaceted circuitry. Hilda points directly to the core component, her silent command clear: take it.
(White Interaction Point: Blood on Chest)

This is the fatal shot. The bullet shattered her brooch, robbing it of its full velocity, but still drove deep into her chest. It didn't exit; it lodged itself inside her. Now, with every ragged breath, she pumps more blood into the cavity of her own body. Saving her is impossible.
She knows it. The fight has already left her eyes.
(Continue with Multiple White Interaction Points)

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: The Monolith... isn't finished... but the remaining data... is enough for the city-state's researchers...
Hilda's voice is a threadbare whisper, each word strained through a bloody froth.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I entrust you... with the spark... beneath... the Monolith...
(Obtained Key 3)
Her voice is a fading whisper, but as your fingers close around the unfinished Monolith she entrusted to you, your own resolve hardens into something cold and sharp.

For all this time, that cipher strip has been an unbreakable lock. You've tried every method, every key, to no avail. But now... now you hold the key to the Monolith itself. If this creation of Hilda's can truly decode any cipher—
There's no time for sentiment. No time to wait for a natural end. With swift, deliberate movements, you take out the cipher strip and slide it into the Monolith's waiting slot.
Hilda's eyes widen in utter disbelief.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...${PlayerName}...

The facade crumbles. In a final, desperate act, her trembling fingers reach for you, not with strength, but with a plea. But the Monolith's work is already done. One by one, the encoded strip unspools into stark, undeniable truth, laying bare the reality she has been so desperate to bury.

June 7. The lockdown directive came in. Cut water and power. I checked the coordinates three times. They were targeting civilian sectors. I reported it. The response was just to follow orders.
This operation resulted in 11 casualties. I'm writing their names here. I have to.

June 9. Filed the raid report.
Operation successful. Another list of names to record.

August 11. Sent the preliminary "mole" report.
15 traitors purged. They were our own. The real mole is still out there.

I questioned it. Got reprimanded, again.
"Obey orders. Fulfill your duty. Don't concern yourself with anything else."
Duty, they say. Duty.
But is my duty just to relay death warrants and watch innocent people die?

September 21. Orders to transport real medical supplies. No cover story this time.
Good. For once, that's a relief.

October 2. Another operation against civilians. I objected.
My first time in solitary. I regret it. Not for speaking up, but because I'll be stuck here for days.
How much intel will I miss?

October 10. Out of confinement.

October 20. A major "error" happened today.
Maybe my hand still isn't steady from the injury. I pressed too hard, smudged the coordinates on the translation.
The strike missed by 5 degrees. Hit nothing but dirt. No casualties.
Our operation failed. And I felt... happy.
I think I'm losing it.
Your consciousness is slipping away. As you clutch the decoded text tightly, emotions surge within you.
So this is it. What she has been hiding all along is a loyalty shattered and remade—not by blind obedience, but by conscience.

Seeing her secret laid bare, Hilda's dying face contorts in despair, her eyes glistening with unshed tears. She doesn't know who you truly are; she believes the cold machinery of the city-state has uncovered her heart. But your answer is to clasp her hand, firmly, in your own.
The darkness presses in, a physical weight. Each breath is a struggle, a shallow gasp in the encroaching void.
Don't worry. Your secret is safe with me. I'll get you... get both of us out of here.
